Note::collapse_punct¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::collapse_punct() const

Reduce Every Run Of Punctuation To Its First Character¶

collapse_punct() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every run of consecutive ASCII punctuation characters in each cell reduced to just its first character. Use it to tame expressive punctuation — "wait...", "really?!?!", "a--b" — before tokenization or display.

The run is defined by the ASCII punctuation class, not by a single repeated mark, so a mixed run collapses too: "?!?!" becomes "?" (the first punctuation character, then the rest of the adjacent punctuation is dropped). Letters, digits, whitespace, and non-ASCII characters are kept exactly and break a run.

collapse_punct is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"wait...", "really?!?!", "a--b__c"}).collapse_punct())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["wait.", "really?", "a-b_c"]

"..." → "."; the mixed run "?!?!" → "?"; "--" → "-" and "__" → "_" because the letters between them break the runs.

See Also¶

  • Note::remove_punctuation: delete punctuation entirely instead of thinning it.

  • Note::collapse_repeats: collapse runs of any identical character, not just punctuation.

  • Note::collapse_whitespace: the whitespace equivalent.
